title: Bounded-latency throughput prover and customer evidence bundle
creator: Ethan Chen
description: Create a deterministic load-testing harness and benchmarking methodology that verifies throughput guarantees and bounded tail latency for Dedicated capacity, produces customer-facing evidence bundles, and integrates autoscaler/fleet-control scenarios into acceptance tests.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity require signed throughput guarantees (QPS and token/sec with P99/P99.9 bounds) and proof from our load labs. Current artifacts are fragmented across legacy harnesses; this ticket consolidates a deterministic prover plus a templated evidence bundle for customer signoff.
approach: Build modular 'bounded-latency prover' composed of: scenario composer (tenant mixes, burst vs steady), deterministic replay runner (seeded RNG for request timing), telemetry collectors (client-side and server-side token traces), and an evidence packager that generates PDFs with charts + telemetry + config. Integrate autoscaler triggers and controlled failure injection to validate fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducible benchmark run that shows throughput >= contract QPS with P99 <= target and P99.9 <= bounded ceiling for three representative tenant mixes
Evidence bundle generated automatically (charts, raw traces, config, git commit) and stored in S3 under customer-evidence/<customer>-<date>
Autoscaler behaves according to policy: scale-up within 60s for sustained surge; no SLA breach during controlled failover to model-variant
Test can be executed by solutions engineer with a single CLI command and documented runbook
Benchmarks include KV cache-hit breakdown and batching efficiency metrics
test_plan: 2) Parameterize request length distributions and prompt shapes (chat vs completion vs embeddings)
3) Run deterministic replay with warmup, ramp, sustain, and cooldown phases; repeat 5 times to build confidence intervals.
4) Capture server telemetry: token throughput, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rate, batch sizes, kernel selection logs.
5) Inject autoscaler events: simulate node removal and forced spike to validate rollback and fallback.
6) Package results and run automated acceptance checks defined in acceptance_criteria.
7) Post results to dashboard and attach evidence bundle to customer folder.
deliverables: scenario catalog (three canonical tenant mixes + JSON templates)
runbook for solutions engineering and customer QA
dashboard view tile showing benchmark comparison vs SLA
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: synthetic traffic may not reflect production cache locality -> Mitigation: include shadow-replay of sampled production traces when available
Risk: GPU kernel nondeterminism under mixed workloads -> Mitigation: pin kernel set and record kernel versions in evidence bundle
Risk: Autoscaler flakiness in CI -> Mitigation: run scale events in isolated lab with controlled capacity and record node-level telemetry
notes: Decisions so far: use deterministic seed replay (rng seed in runner) to make runs reproducible; focus initial run on 2 model families (gpt-open-16k, gpt-open-32k-quant).
Trade-off: longer warmups increase test time but reduce variance — settled on 180s warmup, 600s sustain by default.
Review feedback (PM Maria Gomez): prioritize customer-facing evidence PDF first, then incremental telemetry features.
Dev review (runtime team): need a lightweight agent to pull KV cache hit metrics from runtime API (ENG-42199 is implementing endpoint).
